search_brief.concept_name: Set an ML workload cost guardrail on an existing platform
search_brief.learner_level: Entry/junior-level custom-model and production ML engineering after explicit prerequisite preparation. General computer literacy is required. This is not a native programming-from-zero curriculum: Python and other shared foundations are reused from the immutable global concept registry snapshot, not taught again here. Learners without programming experience must first complete the registry-backed Python preparation route owned by data_analyst. Before the first local Python unit, require its relevant registered foundations: variables and assignment, core types and conversion, operators, strings, conditionals, function definition and return values, default and keyword arguments, variable scope, imports, lists, tuples, dictionaries and sets, collection iteration and comprehensions, for/while loops and loop control, file I/O and exception handling. Prior experience must demonstrate those same prerequisite capabilities; it is not a waiver of them. The local route then teaches ML-specific Python script execution and entry-point structure, structured-data serialization, numerical array shapes/dtypes and bounded dataset ingestion, building on those foundations. SQL foundations are likewise delegated to the registered data_analyst and business_analyst concepts and must be completed before relational ingestion. Foundational statistics/probability, linear algebra and derivatives, and classical-ML problem/metric literacy are explicit prerequisites before modeling; a bounded classical modeling workflow consolidates that literacy here, while deep classical algorithm-selection and research/exploratory modeling belong to the separate Data Scientist path. General software-engineering practice, Git, testing and general CI/CD mechanics are delegated to the Software Engineer prerequisite route before production work, reusing registered equivalents where available. Cloud/container fundamentals and basic infrastructure-as-code knowledge are required before deployment; model-specific Docker packaging, deployment configuration and MLOps CI/CD are taught here. Existing data sources and an authorized cloud/runtime architecture are supplied or accessed through an existing platform: Data Engineer owns upstream ETL/warehouse platforms, Backend Developer owns general API engineering, and DevOps owns broad cloud provisioning. The exit claim is bounded junior ownership under an existing architecture, not the full experienced AWS/Google certification bar. Custom-model training/fine-tuning, serving and operations are required; prompting, RAG, vector databases and LLM/agent orchestration belong to the AI Engineer path. These are curriculum boundaries, not a claim that industry role titles never overlap. A bounded exception to the AI Engineer boundary is owned here: evaluate a supplied foundation-model task solution against a task-specific validation baseline. This is evaluation of supplied outputs and evidence, not construction or integration of a foundation-model application. Managed-service scope is limited to custom-versus-managed decisions using supplied validation evidence and bounded managed custom-model training. Separate AutoML and pretrained-task-API evaluation are deferred, not assessed coverage.
